events.title: 'Black Russian' sabotage group is probably a front, experts suggest

articles.text: 'Black Russian' sabotage group is probably a front, experts suggest Share Follow: Follow LSM on Google Photo: LSM Latgales redakcija Yesterday, 21:04 Defence Authors: Judīte Čunka (Latvian Television) , LSM English (Latvian Public Media) A little-known group called "Black Russians" has claimed responsibility for an incident on the Latvian-Belarusian border in early October, in which masked and armed men attempted to smuggle 20 illegal migrants into the country and later damaged infrastructure, reports Latvian Television. Analysts believe the groups may be a front for hybrid operations created by Belarusian and Russian special services. As previously reported , on the night of October 5th-6th, aggressive and armed men in masks tried to bring 20 illegal migrants from Belarus to Latvia. The escorts threatened soldiers who did not allow them to cross the border. After several hours, the masked people nevertheless entered Latvia and damaged border infrastructure. A little-known group in Belarus called "Чёрные русы" ("Black Russians"), has claimed responsibility for this incident, promising to continue similar operations. Quite why a criminal group would bother to make such a public declaration rather than remain anonymous is an open question. With face covered and voice altered, someone claiming to be called 'Neman', the supposed spokesperson of the "Black Russians" posted a minute-long video on the "Telegram" social media channel. The video says: "We officially assume responsibility for the incident on the Latvian-Belarusian border in Kaplava parish, Krāslava region. We confirm that on the night of October 5th-6th, a group of three "Black Russians" activists crossed the border and engaged in a clash with Latvian soldiers. Then they re-entered Latvian territory near the village of Matuliški, stole video surveillance cameras, damaged the equipment, and remained unnoticed." It is also stated that the "Black Russians" will continue their claimed sabotage against Belarus' neighbors. "It was just a Latvian test that they failed. Soon you will see something similar in other areas of our border. The European Union and NATO are a colossus on feet of clay that will collapse after our first strike," opined 'Neman'. Jānis Sārts, director of the NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence, based in Rīga, suggests that in reality there is no such vigilante group, and that what is happening on the border is an information operation carried out by special services. Such independent groups cannot exist in Belarus and Russia, he insisted. Sarts explained that the purpose was: "To stir up this emotional aspect here, especially for those groups of people who are really worried about it... What is happening on the border is directly related to both the Belarusian and Russian authorities. What they are doing there now is a pure information operation." Sart compared it to a magician's trick, where he performs a trick with one hand and distracts with the other. Dmitry Halko, a Belarusian political refugee and military journalist living in Poland, also shares similar views. "It's some kind of special services project. How real it is physically, we don't know. But it looks like it's some kind of proxy structure, to cover up some kind of activity, to which, if necessary, some events, some sabotage on the borders, and so on, can be attributed. Namely - they're not us, they're some kind of active citizens, so to speak, expressing their position, but we're not to blame here. Well, as usual, they're the little green men, just on a new level. They were green, they became black. It's just a very convenient cover, a very convenient legend for anything. "I think the provocations will continue, we can expect an escalation, even greater than what already exists. And now they have a fig leaf to cover themselves with - it's not us, we don't know anything," said Halko. Latvia's State Security Service (VDD) has drawn attention to a group of individuals based in Belarus who call themselves "Black Russians". On October 9, the VDD initiated criminal proceedings for the creation of a criminal organization with the aim of committing particularly serious crimes against peace, as well as against Latvia and Ukraine. The VDD is currently refraining from comment, however. Seen a mistake? events.title: Record number of illegal border crossing attempts forecast in Latvia

articles.text: Record number of illegal border crossing attempts forecast in Latvia Share Follow: Follow LSM on Google Photo: Aleksejs Dunda Today, 7:12 Defence Authors: LSM English (Latvian Public Media) , Anna Luīze Ruskule (Latgales redakcijas analītiskās pētniecības žurnāliste ) The number of attempted illegal border crossings on the Latvia–Belarus border this year has exceeded the total for the whole of last year – more than 12,000 attempts have been thwarted. Border guards suggest that the 2023 record could also be broken, LSM's Latgale editorial reported on October 12. To date, the highest number of migrants prevented from crossing the border illegally was recorded in 2023 – 13,863 people. The Daugavpils Regional Directorate of the State Border Guard suggests that this record could also be broken this year. Operation Werewolf to run until end of year in Latvia October 6, 18:22 “It is highly likely, if the warm weather persists, because we know that last year, in mid-December, temperatures dropped well below freezing. That brought the situation to an end, but we still have many months and many warm days ahead of us until December. It all depends on the weather conditions and on the determination and organisation of those facilitating migrant movements – their capabilities and the number of people involved. The freezing temperatures in 2021 and 2022 did not deter people from crossing the state border illegally. Some individuals were found to have suffered frostbite. Those individuals subsequently underwent amputations of body parts,” explained Valdis Jukšs, Head of the Daugavpils Administration of the State Border Guard. Border guards are assisted not only by the authorities but also by residents. On Saturday, 10 October, in Asūne parish, Krāslava district, with the help of hunters from Konstantinova, border guards detained eight people without valid travel documents. Border guards continue to work at an increased level, and Operation ‘Vilkatis/Werewolf’ on the Belarusian border has been extended until the end of the year. Seen a mistake?
